{"id":"563fcfaf-3f73-4448-88fb-308b3deeff65","object":"chat.completion","created":1790500392,"model":"deepseek-flash","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"{"requirements":[{"requirement_id":"R1","status":"unsupported","supported_by":[]},{"requirement_id":"R2","status":"partially_supported","supported_by":["C1"]},{"requirement_id":"R3","status":"partially_supported","supported_by":["C1"]},{"requirement_id":"R4","status":"partially_supported","supported_by":["C2","C3"]},{"requirement_id":"R5","status":"unsupported","supported_by":[]},{"requirement_id":"R6","status":"unsupported","supported_by":[]}]}","reasoning_content":"We need answer JSON only. Need evaluate task skeleton requirements with verified claims. Need assign status exactly one per R1-R6. Need not search plan etc. Need use claims C1-C3. Need determine support.

We need parse original question and skeleton. We only have claims:
C1 Sophie (Sophie Xeon), Scottish DJ/producer, died aged 34 on 30 Jan 2021 after accidental fall while watching full moon; accident reported took place in Athens, Greece.
C2 Sophie's partner was Evita Manji.
C3 In later online tribute, Sophie's partner Evita Manji said, "She's an immaterial girl now; she can be anything she wants... and she is in everything around us."

Task requirements:
R1: Charity and first-name relation: musical artist shares first name with part of charity's name; charity unrelated; registered 2000-2010 inclusive.
C1 establishes musical artist first name Sophie. No charity info. unsupported.
R2: Death city and aviation-site relation: artist died in a city 20-30 miles from site of that country's deadliest aviation accident as of 2023. C1 says died after accidental fall in Athens, Greece. Does it establish death city? It says accident took place in Athens, Greece. Need relation to site of Greece's deadliest aviation accident? No. unsupported. Maybe C1 provides death city Athens but no aviation site relation. For requirement, material parts include died in city and distance relation to site. C1 gives death city Athens, but no relation. Is that substantive material part? Requirement is conjunction: death city relation. If it states Athens, that's part? The requirement: "This musical artist died in a city that is 20 to 30 miles away from the site..." It requires city = death city and distance. C1 establishes death city Athens. Is that enough partially_supported? We need consider material parts. It establishes artist died in Athens, so "died in a city" part. But the critical relation is unsupported. The definition partially_supported: verified claims establish at least one substantive material part but one or more remain unsupported. Death in Athens is substantive material part? It is a component. So R2 could be partially_supported supported_by C1. But maybe the requirement is specifically about relation; if no distance, but death city is present. Hmm.

R3: Aviation accident occurred 15 years prior to artist's accidental death. C1 gives artist accidental death 30 Jan 2021. No aviation accident date. unsupported.
R4: Partner interview and song-reference relation: partner at time of death gave interview where they said following death, artist has become a direct reference to one of their songs. C2 partner Evita Manji. C3 later online tribute by partner said "She's an immaterial girl now; she can be anything she wants... and she is in everything around us." Does this establish partner gave interview? "online tribute" not necessarily interview. It said following death? "now" after death? It doesn't say direct reference to a song. It quotes "immaterial girl" maybe lyric/song title? Wait original likely song title "Immaterial" by SOPHIE? The question asks one-word adjective song title. The partner said "She's an immaterial girl now" referencing SOPHIE's song "Immaterial" perhaps. But C3 does not explicitly say "following their death, the artist has become a direct reference to one of their songs." It says "She's an immaterial girl now..." That phrase contains "immaterial", but not claim it's a reference to song. It is a tribute quote, not interview? It says online tribute. So R4 is unsupported? Or partially? It establishes partner at time death (C2) and quote after death, but not interview or direct reference to song. Maybe "online tribute" not interview. The requirement has multiple parts: partner (supported by C2), gave an interview (not supported), said following death, artist has become direct reference to one of their songs (not supported). C3 gives a statement by partner after death but not interview/reference. Does it establish a substantive material part? It establishes partner made a later online tribute including "She's an immaterial girl now" after death. But requirement specifically "gave an interview where they said..." The quote likely is the material content? If C3 says in later online tribute, not interview. So maybe unsupported due to no interview and no song reference. But C3 "immaterial girl" could be direct reference? But not explicit. We must not infer. So maybe unsupported. However C2 establishes partner; that is a material part of R4 ("The partner of the artist at time of death"). But the main requirement is partner interview relation. Partial support? Definition: establish at least one substantive material part. Partner identity is a material part. So R4 partially_supported with C2 and maybe C3? Need decide.

R5: Song title one word, adjective. No claim about song title. unsupported.
R6: Requested song title. Need provide song title. No explicit claim. C3 quote "immaterial" maybe adjective one word, but not stated as song title. Could C3 support that the song title is "Immaterial"? It says "She's an immaterial girl now" not "song title is Immaterial". The original question likely answer "Immaterial". But verified claims don't say. We cannot infer. So unsupported. If R6 asks "What is the song title?" It could be supported if claim states song title. None. unsupported.

Need ensure JSON with requirements. Need assign statuses.

Let's re-read rules: For every Task Requirement, assign exactly one status. For fully_supported, cited claims collectively cover all material content. For partially, at least one substantive material part but not all. For unsupported, supported_by empty.

Need decide R2, R4 partial or unsupported. Need be strict: A Claim supports a Requirement only when Claim materially establishes part of what Requirement requires. R2: "This musical artist died in a city that is 20 to 30 miles (inclusive) away from the site of that country’s deadliest aviation accident (as of 2023)." C1: "died ... after accidental fall ... accident ... took place in Athens, Greece." This establishes the artist died in Athens, Greece (city). It doesn't establish distance to aviation accident site. Does "died in a city" count as substantive material part? The requirement is relational: death city and distance to aviation site. It says artist died in a city that is 20-30 miles from site. To establish part, C1 gives "died in Athens" but not "that is 20-30 miles from site". The city identity might be material because distance depends on city. It is a constituent fact. But if we require relation, maybe no. The status categories allow partial. Usually if claim gives death location but no distance relation, partial support. I'd lean partial_supported for R2 with C1. But need be careful: The requirement says "died in a city that is 20 to 30 miles away from site..." The claim establishes he died in Athens, but not that Athens is 20-30 miles from site. It establishes the "died in a city" component. Is "died in a city" a material semantic condition? Yes. So partial. But is "city" unspecified? It gives Athens. So yes.

R1: no charity, no first name relation. unsupported.
R3: no accident date, but artist accidental death date supported? Requirement: "The aviation accident occurred 15 years prior to the artist’s accidental death." It includes artist accidental death. C1 gives artist accidental death date. Does that count as substantive part? It establishes the artist's accidental death (date) part. The requirement is interval between accident and death. C1 establishes death was accidental and date. But no aviation accident date. So partial? This is similar. The requirement says accident occurred 15 years prior to artist's accidental death. To support, need accident date and death date. C1 gives death date. So at least one material part: death date. Should be partial_supported. But maybe the requirement's material content is only interval: "aviation accident occurred 15 years prior to death." The death event is context. But it's a material part. Under strict partial, yes.

R4: C2 establishes partner identity; C3 quote from partner after death. It may establish partner said something after death. But not interview/direct reference. Partial? likely partially_supported with C2 and C3? Need decide. The requirement: partner of artist (at time death) gave an interview where they said that following their death, the artist has become a direct reference to one of their songs. C2 establishes partner. C3 establishes a later online tribute by partner, with quote "She's an immaterial girl now..." after death? It says "later online tribute" and "now" implies after death. But not interview. It does not say direct reference to song. It does establish partner spoke posthumously. Is that a material part? The core is interview with statement about direct reference to song. Partner identity and post-death statement are parts. So partial. But maybe "online tribute" not interview, but C3 still supports that partner gave a statement after death. The requirement specifically "gave an interview" not any statement. Could be unsupported? The rule: partially if establish at least one substantive material part. Partner identity is material. So partial_supported. If we consider partner identity alone, yes. If we require the partner interview, then no. I'd give partial_supported with C2 and C3? C3 supports that partner made a statement after death, but not interview. It's a substantive part of the relation (partner said something posthumously). However the content "immaterial girl" might be the reference to song? But no explicit. We can cite C2 and C3 as establishing partner and post-death tribute quote. But careful: C3 says "In a later online tribute, Sophie's partner Evita Manji said..." This confirms partner Evita Manji and a later tribute. It doesn't say interview. But supports post-death statement. So partial.

R5: no song title form. unsupported.
R6: no requested song title. unsupported. Could C3 quote "immaterial" support title? It doesn't state title. unsupported.

Need output JSON only. Ensure no extra. Need include requirement_id exactly once.

Let's consider if R2/R3/R4 partial might be considered over-inclusive? The evaluation likely expects rigorous. The task wants statuses based on claims. We need be consistent.

Let's examine original task skeleton labels:
R1 Charity and first-name relation
R2 Death city and aviation-site relation
R3 Accident-to-death interval
R4 Partner interview and song-reference relation
R5 Song-title form
R6 Requested song title

Verified Claims:
C1 Sophie died in Athens
C2 partner Evita Manji
C3 partner quote "She's an immaterial girl now..."

The only possible fully_supported? None. R4 maybe? C3 has "immaterial girl" which might be "direct reference to one of their songs" because the song title is "Immaterial"? But C3 doesn't say direct reference to song. It says "She's an immaterial girl now; she can be anything she wants... and she is in everything around us." This could be a direct reference to song "Immaterial" if we know SOPHIE song "Immaterial" has lyrics "You can be anything you want" etc. But outside knowledge not allowed. Claim itself doesn't mention song. So no.

R6 asks song title. If C3 contains "immaterial", could we infer song title is "Immaterial"? No, not stated. unsupported.

R5 asks one word adjective. C3 has "immaterial" which is an adjective? But no claim it's title. unsupported.

Thus only partials: R2, R3, R4 maybe. R1 unsupported. R5 unsupported. R6 unsupported.

Let's see if R3: C1 gives accidental death. "the artist’s accidental death" is established. The interval "aviation accident occurred 15 years prior" not. So partial. Yes.

R2: C1 gives death city Athens. The relation to aviation accident site not. partial.

R4: C2 gives partner at time of death? It says Sophie's partner was Evita Manji. Does it specify at time of death? Not explicitly, but likely. It doesn't say "at time of death." Could be partner generally. But C3 says "Sophie's partner Evita Manji" in tribute after death. Does that establish partner at time of death? Not necessarily, but maybe. Hmm. R4 requires "partner of the artist (at the time of their death)". C2 just "Sophie's partner was Evita Manji." No temporal qualifier. C3 says "Sophie's partner Evita Manji" in later online tribute. Still not explicitly at time of death. But it's reasonable? The rule says do not infer. If no explicit "at time of death", maybe not fully. But it's a substantive part that Evita Manji was Sophie's partner. We can cite C2. So partial.

C3: "In a later online tribute, Sophie's partner Evita Manji said..." This establishes partner said something later. It does not say interview. The requirement says "gave an interview where they said..." So not interview. But "tribute" is a statement. Partial if we count post-death statement. But is the material part "partner said following death..."? C3 says later online tribute, quote with present tense "now", so yes after death. But not direct reference to song. So partial.

Could R4 be unsupported if partner identity alone isn't enough because requirement is about the partner's interview and statement, not identity? The definition: "establish at least one substantive material part of the requirement." Partner identity is a material part? The phrase "The partner of the artist (at the time of their death)" is a referent. Without it, cannot have interview. But the main predicate is "gave an interview where they said..." If claims only establish that the partner existed, is that a substantive material part? I think yes, because the requirement includes who gave the interview. But perhaps too weak? The rule says entity-name overlap or candidate mention doesn't count. C2 establishes the partner relation explicitly, not mere mention. So it's substantive.

Similarly R2 C1 establishes death city, not relation. R3 C1 establishes death. So partials.

Need decide if R2 supported_by C1 only, R3 C1, R4 C2,C3. R1 none, R5 none, R6 none.

Let's ensure JSON valid. Use exact statuses. No markdown. Final should be JSON object.

Need maybe include "supported_by": [] for unsupported.

Let's produce."},"logprobs":null,"finish_reason":"stop"}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":1257,"completion_tokens":3305,"total_tokens":4562,"prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":1024},"completion_tokens_details":{"reasoning_tokens":3179},"prompt_cache_hit_tokens":1024,"prompt_cache_miss_tokens":233},"system_fingerprint":"aeb56401ca74e127821c4f9126dcb669"}
